sourcedFrom: 1911 Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, 2020 edition (no part code printed; read off the back cover) (2020 ("Copyright 2020. Contents property of Springfield, Inc. All rights reserved."))
cleanIntro: This guide follows Springfield Armory's 1911 Operation & Safety Manual. That book covers Springfield's 1911s by model group and never prints "Range Officer", so check your variant against it. The steps here are the book's full-size section: recoil spring plug and spring first, because the barrel bushing is the only thing holding them, then the slide stop, then the slide forward off the frame with the barrel and recoil parts in it. The book gives a different procedure for its Compact and Champion models (Section 4); if your Range Officer has a shorter slide than the full-size 5-inch gun, follow that section of the book instead.

steps.title: Magazine out first
steps.action: This guide follows Springfield's 1911 manual, which does not name the Range Officer, so check your variant against it. Point the pistol in a safe direction, press the magazine catch and take the magazine out. Wear eye protection from here on: the pistol has parts under spring pressure.
steps.prose: Springfield's disassembly starts with the pistol completely unloaded, magazine and chamber both.
steps.quote: Press magazine catch and remove magazine.
steps.cite: 1911 Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, 2020 edition (no part code printed; read off the back cover) — SECTION 1: DISASSEMBLY, FULL-SIZE MODELS, Step 1, printed p.27
steps.warn: Before performing any cleaning or maintenance, make sure the firearm is completely unloaded (this includes the magazine and chamber). Wear eye protection.

steps.title: Slide back, look in the chamber, let it forward
steps.action: Pull the slide back and look into the chamber to confirm there is no cartridge in it, then release the slide and let it go forward. A round in the chamber stays there when the magazine comes out, so this look is the step that actually proves the pistol empty.
steps.prose: Keep live ammunition out of the area while you work on the pistol.
steps.quote: Pull slide backwards and check that no cartridge is in the chamber.
steps.cite: 1911 Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, 2020 edition (no part code printed; read off the back cover) — SECTION 1: DISASSEMBLY, FULL-SIZE MODELS, Step 1, printed p.27
steps.warn: Never allow live ammunition in the area while you are maintaining your firearm.

steps.title: Two-piece full-length guide rod? Front half out first
steps.action: If your pistol has a two-piece full-length guide rod, unscrew its front portion with a 5/32 Allen wrench before anything else. If it has the short recoil spring guide, there is nothing to do here.
steps.prose: Springfield's full-size section covers both recoil systems and only adds this step for the two-piece rod.
steps.quote: If your pistol contains a 2 piece full length guide rod, use a 5/32 Allen wrench to remove the front portion of guide rod.
steps.cite: 1911 Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, 2020 edition (no part code printed; read off the back cover) — SECTION 1: DISASSEMBLY, FULL-SIZE MODELS, Step 2, printed p.27

steps.title: Slide back half an inch, thumb on the recoil spring plug
steps.action: Rest the butt on your knee and grip the slide behind the front sight. Move the slide back about half an inch, hold it there firmly, and press the recoil spring plug in with your thumb.
steps.prose: The plug sits under the full recoil spring. Your thumb is what keeps it in the slide once the bushing turns.
steps.quote: Move slide rearward, approximately 1/2 inch, grasp firmly to hold in place, and depress recoil spring plug with thumb.
steps.cite: 1911 Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, 2020 edition (no part code printed; read off the back cover) — SECTION 1: DISASSEMBLY, FULL-SIZE MODELS, Step 2, printed p.27
steps.warn: Point muzzle away from face to prevent injury in the event plug is ejected by spring.

steps.title: Muzzle away from your face, bushing clockwise
steps.action: With the muzzle pointed away from your face, turn the barrel bushing clockwise. Do not turn it off the plug until you have the plug and spring under control.
steps.prose: If the bushing clears the plug while your thumb is not on it, the plug leaves at speed.
steps.quote: Point muzzle away from face and rotate barrel bushing clockwise.
steps.cite: 1911 Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, 2020 edition (no part code printed; read off the back cover) — SECTION 1: DISASSEMBLY, FULL-SIZE MODELS, Step 2, printed p.27
steps.warn: Do not rotate bushing off of plug unless you have control of plug and spring.

steps.title: Let the plug and spring come forward slowly
steps.action: Ease the plug and recoil spring forward under your thumb rather than letting go of them.
steps.prose: Nothing should snap free here. If it does, the bushing came off the plug before you had control.
steps.quote: Cautiously allow plug and recoil spring to move forward.
steps.cite: 1911 Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, 2020 edition (no part code printed; read off the back cover) — SECTION 1: DISASSEMBLY, FULL-SIZE MODELS, Step 3, printed p.28

steps.title: Line the disassembly notch up with the slide stop
steps.action: Move the slide back until the disassembly notch on the slide sits over the slide stop.
steps.prose: The slide stop only comes out at this one slide position. If it will not move, the notch is not lined up yet.
steps.quote: Align disassembly notch on slide with slide stop.
steps.cite: 1911 Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, 2020 edition (no part code printed; read off the back cover) — SECTION 1: DISASSEMBLY, FULL-SIZE MODELS, Step 4, printed p.28

steps.title: Push the shaft from the right, pull the slide stop out the left
steps.action: Press the slide stop's shaft where it shows on the right side of the frame, and draw the slide stop out of the left side.
steps.prose: Do not pry the slide stop out. If it is hard to move, recheck the notch alignment from the step before.
steps.quote: Press slide stop shaft on right side of frame and remove slide stop by pulling it out of left side of frame.
steps.cite: 1911 Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, 2020 edition (no part code printed; read off the back cover) — SECTION 1: DISASSEMBLY, FULL-SIZE MODELS, Step 4, printed p.28

steps.title: Slide forward off the frame
steps.action: Pull the slide forward along its guides and off the frame. The barrel, barrel bushing, recoil spring plug, recoil spring and guide all come away with it.
steps.prose: The frame is now on its own. Everything still to come apart is in the slide.
steps.quote: Pull slide forward in its guides and remove slide. Barrel, barrel bushing, recoil spring plug, recoil spring and guide will come with it.
steps.cite: 1911 Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, 2020 edition (no part code printed; read off the back cover) — SECTION 1: DISASSEMBLY, FULL-SIZE MODELS, Step 5, printed p.29

steps.title: Recoil spring and guide out the back
steps.action: Take the recoil spring and its guide out through the rear of the slide.
steps.prose: Keep them together. On reassembly the guide and spring must line up with the barrel before they go back into the slide.
steps.quote: Remove recoil spring and guide through back side.
steps.cite: 1911 Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, 2020 edition (no part code printed; read off the back cover) — SECTION 1: DISASSEMBLY, FULL-SIZE MODELS, Step 6, printed p.29

steps.title: Bushing to the left and out the front
steps.action: Turn the barrel bushing to the left of the slide and take it out through the front.
steps.prose: The bushing turns the opposite way to the clockwise turn that released the plug.
steps.quote: Rotate barrel bushing to left of slide and remove it through the front.
steps.cite: 1911 Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, 2020 edition (no part code printed; read off the back cover) — SECTION 1: DISASSEMBLY, FULL-SIZE MODELS, Step 7, printed p.29

steps.title: Field strip complete: barrel out the front
steps.action: Tilt the barrel link forward and slide the barrel out of the front of the slide. That is the field strip: frame, slide, barrel, bushing, plug, recoil spring and guide. The firing pin and extractor work the book gives is under DEEP CLEAN.
steps.prose: Springfield's full-size section ends here and reassembles by reversing these steps.
steps.quote: Tilt barrel link forward and remove barrel from front of slide.
steps.cite: 1911 Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, 2020 edition (no part code printed; read off the back cover) — SECTION 1: DISASSEMBLY, FULL-SIZE MODELS, Step 7, printed p.29
steps.warn: Improper disassembly may damage the firearm. Always consult an experienced gunsmith if you experience any difficulty or have any questions concerning assembly procedure.

deepSteps.title: Firing pin stop out: back of the slide away from your face
deepSteps.action: With the slide off, press the firing pin in with a pin punch while you push the firing pin tail past the firing pin stop, then pull the stop down out of the slide.
deepSteps.prose: The firing pin is under its spring. Keep the back end of the slide, where the pin comes out, pointed away from your face.
deepSteps.quote: If necessary, remove firing pin by pressing it with pin punch while simultaneously pushing firing pin tail past the firing pin stop, then pull firing pin stop downward from slide.
deepSteps.cite: 1911 Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, 2020 edition (no part code printed; read off the back cover) — PERIODIC CLEANING: EXTRACTOR, Step 1, printed p.61
deepSteps.warn: Point the back end of the slide, where the firing pin exits, away from face to prevent injury in the event the firing pin is ejected by the spring.

deepSteps.title: Firing pin and spring out
deepSteps.action: Take the firing pin and its spring out of the back of the slide.
deepSteps.prose: Springfield says this can be done once the slide is off the frame.
deepSteps.quote: Remove firing pin and its spring.
deepSteps.cite: 1911 Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, 2020 edition (no part code printed; read off the back cover) — PERIODIC CLEANING: EXTRACTOR, Step 1, printed p.61

deepSteps.title: Extractor out by the firing pin stop groove
deepSteps.action: With a pin punch, draw the extractor out of the slide by the groove the firing pin stop runs in.
deepSteps.prose: This is the last removal the book gives. It does not go any further into the slide or into the frame.
deepSteps.quote: Using pin punch, pull extractor by groove where firing pin stop runs.
deepSteps.cite: 1911 Operation & Safety Manual — Operation & Safety Manual, 2020 edition (no part code printed; read off the back cover) — PERIODIC CLEANING: EXTRACTOR, Step 2, printed p.61

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBER
tasks: Cleaning rod in from the chamber end where you can, pushed all the way out the muzzle
Solvent-wetted patch through the barrel several times
Solvent-wetted bristle brush run the full length of the bore until clean
Dry patches, then look the barrel over; scrub again if needed
Do not reverse the rod while a patch or brush is in the barrel; it can bind
Finish with a dry patch, then one lightly-oiled patch

cleaning.name: SLIDE, BREECH FACE & EXTRACTOR
tasks: Bristle brush and solvent on the breech face and extractor
Powder residue off with powder solvent on a clean patch
Scrubbed areas wiped with a solvent-wetted patch
Work carefully with a brush so you do not damage parts

cleaning.name: FRAME
tasks: Powder residue off the frame's components with solvent on a patch, or a solvent-wetted bristle brush
If the lower parts are especially dirty, take the grip panels off before soaking or flushing them in solvent
Get all the dirt and solvent out afterwards, then oil lightly

cleaning.name: MAGAZINES
tasks: Bristle brush on the magazine lips and follower
Old grease cleaned out of the magazine
Lips checked for nicks, burrs or deformation

cleaning.name: OIL
tasks: All surfaces wiped clean with a cloth, then with a lightly-oiled patch or cloth
Only a very small amount of oil; stainless pistols need slightly more than blued or parkerized ones
Do not use patches dripping with solvent or oil
Heavier final oil only if the pistol is going into long storage

reassembly: Reassemble by reversing the order of disassembly.
Barrel into the front of the slide, then the barrel bushing in through the front and turned back into place.
Recoil spring and guide in through the rear of the slide, lined up with the barrel before they go in.
Flip the barrel link forward before the slide goes onto the frame.
Slide onto the frame rails and back until the disassembly notch meets the slide stop hole; slide stop in from the left, its shaft through the hole in the barrel link.
Recoil spring plug in over the spring under your thumb and the bushing turned over it, muzzle away from your face.
Two-piece full-length guide rod (if fitted): front portion back in with the 5/32 Allen wrench.
fncheck: Magazine out, chamber empty, muzzle in a safe direction. Work the slide by hand several times and check it runs fully forward and back without binding, and that the slide stop is seated through the barrel link. Springfield's warning is plain: an improperly assembled firearm is dangerous and should not be fired. If anything did not go back the way it came out, take the pistol to an experienced gunsmith before shooting it.
